1.title: Calcareous Sandstone: The Generous Dryness of the Triassic
1.html: The calcareous sandstone (calcaro-gréseux) family is made of Triassic (Trias) calcareous sandstone, relatively poor but extremely well-drained. The shared feature of these three sites is an unusually dry microclimate — an excellent cradle for Alsace noble-rot and late-harvest wines.
2.title: The Three Calcareous Sandstone Stars
2.items.0.label: Geisberg (Ribeauvillé, 8.53 ha)
2.items.0.desc: Lower Muschelkalk dolomite / dolomitic marl, a steep slope requiring terraced farming. Documented as early as 1308. Riesling's "terre d'élection" (land of choice) — it has developed a famously intense minerality and is a pilgrimage site for Riesling lovers.
2.items.1.label: Pfingstberg (Orschwihr, 28.15 ha)
2.items.1.desc: Upper calcareous sandstone plus micaceous sandstone (base of the Muschelkalk, top of the Buntsandstein), with more clayey sandstone below, so it is subdivided into the two small place names Pfingstberg and Lippelsberg. Documented in 1299. Gewurztraminer, Riesling, Pinot Gris and Muscat, intensely floral; Riesling needs 1–2 years in bottle to show fully.
2.items.2.label: Zinnkoepflé (Soultzmatt & Westhalten, 71.03 ha)
2.items.2.desc: The "roof of the Alsace vineyards" — up to 420 m, Triassic calcareous sandstone, anciently called "Vallis Prænobilis" (the noble valley). Shielded by the Petit and Grand Ballon, it is one of the driest areas of Alsace. Gewurztraminer, the "king of Alsace wines", shows extreme power here, while Riesling unexpectedly shows delicacy and harmony.
3.question: Which site is called the "roof of the Alsace vineyards" and is the representative site for Gewurztraminer's extreme power?
3.options.2: Zinnkoepflé — up to 420 m, and shielded by the mountains, making it one of the driest areas of Alsace
3.explanation: Zinnkoepflé (Soultzmatt & Westhalten) reaches 420 m and is called the "roof of the Alsace vineyards". Shielded by the Petit Ballon and Grand Ballon, it has an extremely dry, hot microclimate and is the representative site where Gewurztraminer, the "king of Alsace wines", shows power and spice, while Riesling unexpectedly shows delicacy and harmony.
